b9afb3d5d95093d4ba33fa8d7183e90484081c11: Flumet offers 90 km of well-marked runs, an intermediate-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 36 lifts are generally sufficient to absorb the crowds in high season. Flumet's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Flumet's altitude (1000 m at the bottom, 2070 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it is best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The day lift pass at 41€ places Flumet among the mid-range resorts on price: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Flumet is one of those rare resorts that combines a real village, a sincere family atmosphere and runs suited to everyone. It would be hard to miss your stay here.

b9d78ee9ddcc032b89686ee87a2d47a22f89885c: Human-scale, Galtür focuses on warm welcome and closeness rather than impressive figures. Its 43 km of runs are ideal for a 3- to 4-day stay, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Technical terrain is king at Galtür: with 28 black and 58 red runs on offer, confirmed skiers will find plenty to challenge them. Off-piste and freeride are often enjoyed in excellent conditions thanks to the altitude and the orientation of the slopes. Galtür's altitude (1,600 m at the base, 2,300 m at the top) allows it to maintain reasonable snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it's best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay at Galtür is clearly high: 63€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Galtür doesn't compete with the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
